_comment: Byte ceiling and parser cap for the self-hosted hook bundle (dist/hooks/dispatch.js). Registered by road-to-a-hook-bundle-with-one-yaml-reader step 2.1. Read by src/scripts/check_hook_bundle_composition.ts, which builds the bundle from source with --metafile and compares. WHY A CEILING AT ALL: every concern is inlined into one bundle that every hook event loads, so a dependency added for one concern is paid by all of them, on every dispatch. The second YAML parser that opened this roadmap cost 95,846 bytes and reached a release as a review finding rather than as a red check. A ceiling makes the next one a red check.
max_bytes_derivation: Measured 1,514,715 bytes on origin/main at 213d87055 (the gate's own reading, APFS-cloned node_modules so no worktree path artefacts). The ceiling is that reading plus ~2.3 % of headroom, rounded to 1,550,000, on the same doctrine as the 2026-10-01 registration: a bundle is rebuilt from source on every run, so an esbuild minor that renames symbols moves the figure by hundreds of bytes with no change to this tree, and a ceiling one byte above the reading would red on that. Composition is healthy at this reading and was checked rather than assumed: one YAML package (258,833 bytes) and 1,238,525 bytes of own source, so the growth is own code, not a re-entered dependency. The 1,564,211-byte pre-swap regression this roadmap closed still cannot reappear under it. RAISED 2026-10-11 to 1,575,000: the reading with the SVG rules present is 1,562,931 B, plus the same ~0.8 % of headroom the original derivation allowed for an esbuild symbol-rename, rounded. Composition is unchanged at one YAML reader; the growth is own source, not a re-entered dependency.
shrink_only_note: A RAISE needs a recorded reason in `raise_log` below naming what was added and why it could not be avoided. Enforced since road-to-a-ratification-fence-that-follows-its-imports 3.2: the gate reads `max_bytes` at the base revision, and a working value above it fails unless `raise_log` gained an entry whose `to` equals the new value. A lowering needs no entry. This file is also on the ratification gate's watched set, so a raise carries a record as well as a log entry.

raise_log.what_was_added: Nothing in this commit. The 1,500,000 ceiling was red on the very commit that registered it: measured 1,511,489 bytes at 22b19e520, which is the merge of the PR that introduced the budget. Its derivation read 1,469,738 bytes on the PR branch, whose base predated three PRs that had merged meanwhile — the failure-event binding of #2160 (sixteen concerns on a new slot), the touched-file quality pass of #2152, and the evidence classification of #2153 — and #2162 landed after it. The gate ran on each PR's pre-merge tree and never on the merge result, so every one of those PRs was green alone and the trunk was red the moment they were together.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: The bytes are deliberately merged capability, not an accident to trim: the composition check above shows one parser and no duplicate dependency, so there is nothing to remove that would not remove a feature. The alternative — reverting a merged lane to fit a ceiling derived against a base that no longer exists — would discard working code to satisfy a number that never described this tree.
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Measuring the ceiling against the merge result rather than the PR branch. A ceiling derived on a branch is a statement about that branch; the trunk is what the gate defends, and the two diverge exactly when several lanes land in one day.

raise_log.what_was_added: The SVG rule set, reached by the design pass. Step 1.4 routes an `.svg` write to `lint_svg_asset`'s findings inside `design_pass_hook` only, because that hook already fired on an `.svg` inside a UI tree and then scanned it with `lint_design_slop`, which holds zero SVG rules — it reached the pass and learned nothing — while an `.svg` outside a UI tree never reached it at all. Measured on this branch: the bundle reads 1,532,007 B with the import stubbed out and 1,571,574 B with the whole linter imported, so the module cost 39,567 B and took the bundle 21,574 B past the 1,550,000 ceiling.
raise_log.why_it_could_not_be_avoided: Most of it was avoided, and the part that was not is the capability itself. Splitting the rule set out of the CLI — `_lib/svg_rules.ts`, with the argv parsing, the directory walk, the project-config reader, the scanned-nothing guard and the preservation readout left behind in `lint_svg_asset.ts` — reclaimed 8,643 B and brought the bundle to 1,562,931 B. The remaining 12,931 B is the rules: five families (structure, safety graded per delivery mode, vector honesty, accessibility, motion), each of which the fixture corpus shows finding a planted defect no existing instrument reads. The only further lever is shortening the finding messages, which are the part a consumer actually acts on — that would trade the product for the number. Two alternatives were considered and rejected on evidence rather than taste: loading the rules from disk at dispatch time fails in a consumer install, where the hook runs from `dist/hooks/dispatch.js` and the TypeScript source is not shipped; and widening `UI_EXTENSIONS` instead would route every asset write through `ui_route_nudge_hook` as well, which costs tokens on every dispatch rather than bytes once (decision E10, Risk 4).
raise_log.what_would_have_caught_it: Nothing earlier: the step that adds the import is the step that spends the bytes, and the gate caught it at the first push, which is where it is supposed to. What the roadmap itself missed is that step 1.4 had a byte cost at all — it accounted for the token cost of widening the UI predicate and not for the bundle cost of the import it chose instead. A roadmap step that adds an import to a hook should name this budget the way step 3.1 named the estate budget.

max_yaml_packages_note: The dispatch path reads YAML for the hook manifest, the host-lowering table and the settings contract. One reader covers all three. Two cost 95,846 bytes for a single call site and were invisible until an external rescore counted them — which is why this is a cap rather than prose. The package set the cap counts over is YAML_PACKAGES in the gate.
what_this_does_not_bound: Latency. A smaller bundle is not a measured speed-up; src/config/hook-latency-budget.json owns the wall-clock axis and is not derived from this file. Nor does it bound dist/install/install.mjs or dist/mcp/server.mjs, which carry their own module graphs.
